Multistate model for one treatment group

Source: R/ms_model.R
ms_model.Rd

Defines the multistate model of one group: progression-free and alive (state 1), progressed without switch (state 2), switched (state 3) and dead (state 4), and, when switch_pre is positive, progression-free after a switch before progression (state 5). Progression-free survival (PFS) is the time to leave the progression-free states and overall survival (OS) is the time to enter state 4.

Usage

ms_model(
  time = 0,
  prog = 0,
  death,
  death_prog = NULL,
  switch_prob = 0,
  switch_rate = 0,
  death_switch = NULL,
  dropout = 0,
  time_post = 0,
  clock = c("reset", "forward"),
  switch_clock = c("same", "switch"),
  switch_af = NULL,
  switch_pre = 0,
  prog_switch = NULL,
  death_switch_pre = NULL,
  dropout_pfs = 0
)

Arguments

time

Interval start times for the pre-progression intensities and the dropout hazard. Must start at 0 and be strictly increasing.

prog

Progression hazard in each interval (length 1 or length(time)).

death

Hazard of death before progression in each interval.

death_prog

Hazard of death after progression without switch, in each interval of time_post. Required when prog is positive in some interval.

switch_prob

Probability of switching immediately at progression, in each interval of time.

switch_rate

Hazard of switching after progression, in each interval of time_post.

death_switch

Hazard of death after a switch, in each interval of time_post. Defaults to death_prog, that is, switching has no effect on survival.

dropout

Dropout hazard in each interval of time.

time_post

Interval start times for the post-progression intensities. Must start at 0 and be strictly increasing.

clock

Clock of the post-progression intensities: "reset" (time since progression) or "forward" (time since randomization).

switch_clock

Clock of death_switch: "same" (the clock of the other post-progression intensities) or "switch" (time since the switch).

switch_af

Acceleration factor of an accelerated failure time effect of the switch (positive), or NULL (default) for the hazard death_switch. When given, death_switch must not be given and switch_clock must be "same".

switch_pre

Hazard of switching before progression, in each interval of time.

prog_switch

Hazard of progression after a switch before progression, in each interval of time. Defaults to prog.

death_switch_pre

Hazard of death before progression after a switch, in each interval of time. Defaults to death.

dropout_pfs

Hazard of a censoring of PFS only, in each interval of time.

Value

An object of class ms_model: a list with the intensity vectors expanded to the lengths of time and time_post, clock, switch_clock, switch_af and pfs_switch ("event"; set by ms_scenario). With switch_af, the element death_switch holds switch_af * death_prog, the death hazard after a switch when death_prog is constant.

Details

Before progression, the intensities are piecewise constant in the time since randomization, with intervals starting at time: progression (prog), death before progression (death), and the probability switch_prob of switching immediately at progression (evaluated at the time of progression). After progression without switch, the patient dies with intensity death_prog or switches with intensity switch_rate; after a switch, the patient dies with intensity death_switch. The post-progression intensities are piecewise constant with intervals starting at time_post.

With clock = "reset" (default) the post-progression intensities are functions of the time since progression (a semi-Markov model). With clock = "forward" they are functions of the time since randomization (a Markov model). The two clocks give the same model when the post-progression intensities are constant.

The death hazard after a switch at the post-progression clock value \(\sigma\) is, at the clock value \(\tau\), death_switch at \(\tau\) with switch_clock = "same" (default), and death_switch at \(\tau - \sigma\) (the time since the switch) with switch_clock = "switch". With clock = "reset" the two differ only for switches after progression (switch_rate); with clock = "forward" they differ also for switches at progression. With switch_af given, the effect of a switch is an accelerated failure time effect: the death hazard after the switch is \(\phi c(\sigma + \phi (\tau - \sigma))\), where \(\phi\) is switch_af and \(c\) is death_prog, so that the remaining time is that without switch divided by \(\phi\) (the rank preserving structural failure time model of Robins and Tsiatis 1991; \(\phi < 1\) prolongs survival).

A switch before progression moves a patient from state 1 to state 5 with hazard switch_pre. In state 5 the patient progresses with hazard prog_switch and dies with hazard death_switch_pre; at progression the patient enters state 3 and then dies with the hazard death_switch on the post-progression clock, whatever switch_clock (with switch_af, the hazard switch_af * death_prog). Whether a switch before progression censors PFS is set in ms_scenario (pfs_switch).

Dropout is piecewise exponential with intervals starting at time, independent of the event process, and censors both endpoints. The hazard dropout_pfs adds a censoring that acts on PFS only (for example the end of tumor assessments), independent of everything else.

A model without progression (prog = 0) is a piecewise exponential model for a single endpoint with hazard death. With death_prog = death, switch_prob = 0 and switch_rate = 0, the model is that of Fleischer et al. (2009); see ms_fleischer.

References

Fleischer F, Gaschler-Markefski B, Bluhmki E (2009). A statistical model for the dependence between progression-free survival and overall survival. Statistics in Medicine 28:2669-2686.

Robins JM, Tsiatis AA (1991). Correcting for non-compliance in randomized trials using rank preserving structural failure time models. Communications in Statistics - Theory and Methods 20:2609-2631.

See also

ms_fleischer, ms_scenario, ms_surv, ms_prob

Examples

# Single endpoint: exponential survival with a median of 12 months
ms_model(death = log(2) / 12)
#> Four-state model for one group (clock after progression: "reset")
#> Before progression (time since randomization):
#>  time prog      death switch_prob dropout
#>     0    0 0.05776227           0       0

# Progression, with 30 percent of the patients switching at progression
ms_model(time = c(0, 6), prog = c(0.10, 0.08), death = 0.01,
         death_prog = 0.05, switch_prob = 0.3, death_switch = 0.03)
#> Four-state model for one group (clock after progression: "reset")
#> Before progression (time since randomization):
#>  time prog death switch_prob dropout
#>     0 0.10  0.01         0.3       0
#>     6 0.08  0.01         0.3       0
#> After progression (time since progression):
#>  time_post death_prog switch_rate death_switch
#>          0       0.05           0         0.03

# Switching after progression with an accelerated failure time effect
ms_model(prog = 0.1, death = 0.01, death_prog = 0.05, switch_rate = 0.04,
         switch_af = 0.7)
#> Four-state model for one group (clock after progression: "reset")
#> Before progression (time since randomization):
#>  time prog death switch_prob dropout
#>     0  0.1  0.01           0       0
#> After progression (time since progression):
#>  time_post death_prog switch_rate death_switch
#>          0       0.05        0.04        0.035
#> Death after a switch: accelerated failure time effect with factor 0.7 ('death_switch' is 0.7 * death_prog).

# Switching before progression, and censoring of PFS only
ms_model(prog = 0.1, death = 0.01, death_prog = 0.05, death_switch = 0.03,
         switch_pre = 0.02, dropout_pfs = 0.01)
#> Five-state model for one group (clock after progression: "reset")
#> Before progression (time since randomization):
#>  time prog death switch_prob dropout dropout_pfs
#>     0  0.1  0.01           0       0        0.01
#> Switch before progression (time since randomization):
#>  time switch_pre prog_switch death_switch_pre
#>     0       0.02         0.1             0.01
#> After progression (time since progression):
#>  time_post death_prog switch_rate death_switch
#>          0       0.05           0         0.03
